title: Toddler Literacy
subject: Literacy
philosophy: Literacy begins with listening, talking, singing and sharing stories. Toddlers learn language by hearing it used warmly and often, by joining in rhymes and songs, by handling books and by making marks. ELA’s Toddler Literacy builds a strong oral foundation and early sound awareness, so that later reading and writing rest on secure listening, vocabulary and confidence. It does not rush letters or handwriting.
rationale: Children who arrive at formal phonics with rich vocabulary, sharp listening and a love of stories learn to read more easily. This programme gives toddlers daily experiences of environmental sounds, rhythm, rhyme, syllables and first sounds, together with picture books, Nigerian stories and songs, and plenty of large, playful mark-making. It follows ELA’s phonics sequence, where Toddler is the listening phase and the first four sounds are heard and said, not written.
aims: To build listening skills and attention through sounds, songs and stories.
To grow vocabulary and spoken sentences in English while valuing children’s home languages.
To develop awareness of rhythm, rhyme, syllables and first sounds.
To share books and stories with enjoyment, naming and talking about pictures.
To strengthen the large and small movements that lead to writing, and to encourage confident mark-making.
learningOutcomes: Listens to a short story or song and responds with words, gestures or actions.
Names familiar people, objects, foods and animals, and uses simple sentences of two to four words.
Joins in action rhymes and songs and fills in missing words.
Tells sounds apart: loud and quiet, high and low, animal and instrument sounds.
Claps the syllables of a name and recognises words that rhyme with support.
Hears and says the first sound of a few familiar words (s, a, t, p) in games.
Handles a book correctly, turns pages and points to and names pictures.
Makes large and small marks, patterns and lines with crayons, chalk, fingers and sand.
Recognises own name card and the first letter of own name with support.
developmentalExpectations: Spoken language develops at different speeds; understanding comes before speaking.
Children learn through repetition, so favourite songs and stories are repeated many times.
Listening for sounds is a skill that must be taught and practised in short, playful bursts.
Pre-writing starts with the whole arm, then the hand, then the fingers. Pencil grip is not expected.
Home languages are a strength. Teachers welcome them and link them to English words.
keyCompetencies: Attentive listening and following simple instructions.
Expressive speech: words, phrases and short sentences.
Joining in with songs, rhymes and stories.
Sound awareness: rhythm, rhyme, syllables and first sounds.
Early book and print awareness and large mark-making.

strands.title: Listening and sound awareness
strands.description: Environmental sounds, voice sounds, loud and quiet, rhythm and body percussion.

strands.title: Speaking and vocabulary
strands.description: Names, greetings, naming objects, simple sentences, questions and answers.

strands.title: Rhymes, songs and stories
strands.description: Action rhymes, nursery rhymes, retelling stories, sequencing pictures.

strands.title: Phonological awareness
strands.description: Rhyme, syllables and first sounds (s, a, t, p) heard and said.

strands.title: Books and print
strands.description: Handling books, naming pictures, noticing print, name cards and first letters.

strands.title: Mark-making and pre-writing
strands.description: Finger play, big marks, patterns and lines, and making a first book.

priorKnowledge: None assumed. Children may know songs from home. Observe in the first two weeks how each child listens, speaks and handles books, and record it as the baseline.
yearProgression: Term 1 builds listening, voice and vocabulary: sounds around us, loud and quiet, animal and instrument sounds, greetings and names, action rhymes, picture books and naming things.
Term 2 builds sound play and early print: rhyme, syllables, finger strength, big mark-making, vocabulary themes, songs, retelling and questions, and noticing print.
Term 3 introduces the first sounds s, a, t and p as listening and speaking games, develops pre-writing patterns, two-step instructions, story sequencing, own name and a first handmade book.
assessmentPrinciples: Assessment is by watching, listening and recording what children say and do during play and stories. There are no written tests.
Levels Emerging, Developing, Secure and Exceeding follow the lesson success criteria (see ASSESSMENT_FRAMEWORK.md).
Record exact words children use now and then, to show growth in language over the year.
Share with parents in plain language, always with a strength, a next step and a home idea.
inclusion: Every lesson has a support and an extension version.
Use gesture, pictures, objects and songs together so children with different strengths can take part.
Accept home-language words and repeat them in English in a natural way.
For children who speak little, value pointing, sounds and actions and give extra time.
crossCurricular: Numeracy: counting rhymes, patterns and sorting books by size.
Science: listening walks, animals, my body and the senses.
Social Habits: greetings, turn-taking, listening manners and sharing books.
EYFS mapping: Communication and Language and Literacy, with Expressive Arts and Design and Physical Development (see STANDARDS_ALIGNMENT.md).
parentConnection: Every lesson ends with a short home idea using talk, songs, books or objects at home.
Parents are encouraged to talk, sing and read together every day, in any language they use at home.
Families are invited to lend a favourite song, story or rhyme from their own language and culture.

objectives: Children will stop, listen and say or show what they hear.
Children will match a sound to the thing that makes it with support.
expectedOutcomes: Stays still to listen for a short time.
Names or points to the source of a familiar sound.

objectives: Children will make a loud and a quiet sound on request.
Children will use their voices in play, such as a whisper and a shout.
expectedOutcomes: Changes the loudness of their voice on request.
Uses a voice sound to join a game.

objectives: Children will match animal pictures to sounds.
Children will make animal sounds and say the animal name.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least three animals.
Makes the sound of a familiar animal.

objectives: Children will copy a short beat with an instrument or their body.
Children will say fast or slow with support.
expectedOutcomes: Copies a two-beat pattern.
Plays an instrument gently.

subtopics: My name and my friends’ names
objectives: Children will say or sign a greeting to an adult or friend.
Children will say or point to their own name and a friend’s name.
expectedOutcomes: Greets someone with a word or wave.
Responds to their own name.

objectives: Children will join in actions and words of a short rhyme.
Children will fill in a missing word with support.
expectedOutcomes: Joins in at least two rhymes with actions.
Says the last word of a line when the teacher pauses.

subtopics: Holding a book and turning pages
objectives: Children will hold a book the right way up and turn pages.
Children will point to and name pictures.
expectedOutcomes: Turns pages one at a time with support.
Names three pictures in a book.

objectives: Children will name familiar people, foods and objects.
Children will say a word or two to ask for something.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least ten familiar things.
Uses two words together to ask for something.

subtopics: Joining in with a repeated line
objectives: Children will listen to a story with pictures and objects.
Children will join in with a repeated line and actions.
expectedOutcomes: Listens to a short story.
Joins in with a repeated line.

objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with confidence at play stations.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.

subtopics: Hearing words that sound the same at the end
objectives: Children will notice when two words rhyme.
Children will finish a familiar rhyme with a rhyming word.
expectedOutcomes: Says the rhyming word in a familiar rhyme.
Matches two pictures that rhyme with support.

objectives: Children will clap the beats in their name.
Children will clap the beats in simple words.
expectedOutcomes: Claps the beats in their own name.
Matches a word to the number of claps with support.

objectives: Children will squeeze, pinch and poke playdough and sponges.
Children will thread large objects with support.
expectedOutcomes: Squeezes and rolls playdough.
Threads at least one large bead.

subtopics: Chalk and water on the ground
objectives: Children will make marks with fingers, chalk and crayons.
Children will say what their marks show.
expectedOutcomes: Makes marks with a tool.

objectives: Children will name fruits, vegetables and market things.
Children will ask for something using a short phrase.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least six fruits or vegetables.
Uses a short phrase to ask for an item.

objectives: Children will sing and do actions to a song.
Children will remember words of a favourite song.
expectedOutcomes: Sings along with several songs.
Does the right action at the right word.

objectives: Children will retell a short story using props or puppets.
Children will use words such as first, then and the end.
expectedOutcomes: Retells part of a story with props.
Uses a story word.

objectives: Children will answer simple who, what and where questions.
Children will ask a simple question such as "What is that?"
expectedOutcomes: Answers who, what and where questions with a word or phrase.
Asks one question.

objectives: Children will notice print on signs, labels and books.
Children will recognise their own name card with support.
expectedOutcomes: Points to print and says what it is for.
Finds their own name card among three.

objectives: Children will show Term 2 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 2 record.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar tasks with growing independence.

Points to an object that starts with /s/.

expectedOutcomes: Says /t/ and /p/ clearly.
